1) Access controls (RBAC / least privilege), you asked how roles map to request types (admin / support / read-only). Vivek is pulled in to add the role matrix and examples.
2) Support access & break-glass, we discussed time-limited support sessions vs. console-only audit-led access. Priyom will share our break-glass playbook and logging controls.
3) Data residency & retention, we covered regional host options and retention TTLs; attached our policy summary.
4) Evidence & artifacts, Emily requested SOC2 evidence and a short network diagram for your security intake.

Next steps (proposed):
- Vivek to send RBAC role matrix and sample IAM policies (by Tue EOD PT).
- Priyom to share break-glass / support access procedure and sample audit logs (by Wed).

Thanks, if that works I'll lock the calendar.

Marissa

Thanks Marissa, that recap looks good. A few clarifications from our side:

- For RBAC, we're most concerned about ensuring support engineers can only access logs/metadata and never raw PII. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports scoping support sessions to redacted views?
- For break-glass, we need details on who is authorized to trigger, how approvals are recorded, and how those sessions are audited. Can you provide a sample audit log entry format?
- On data residency: FinCo requires EU residency for EU customer data; please confirm whether Redwood can guarantee region-locked storage and separate keying per region.

I've copied procurement for timeline alignment — we aim to finish security review this week and move to SOW prep.

Emily Chen
Director, Security & Privacy | FinCo Payments
emily.chen@fincopay.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@fincopay.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data access controls / support access follow-ups

Emily, quick answers and I'll attach the role matrix and examples in a follow-up: 

- Redaction/scoped views: Our console supports field-level redaction for logs and stored request payloads; we can provision a support role that only sees metadata and redacted payloads. For customers requiring strict separation, we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching with PII-hashed keys (we'll include policy notes).
- Break-glass: We operate a time-limited just-in-time access flow. Trigger requires two-step approval for production (on-call engineer + customer security approver). All sessions are captured with a support-ticket ID, session start/end timestamp, operator id, and a base64-hashed snapshot of affected keys. Example log line attached.
- Region keying: We support region-locked storage and customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) per region. That gives you separate encryption domains for EU vs US.

I'm attaching the RBAC matrix (CSV) and a sample audit-log snippet. Priyom: can you add the break-glass runbook and a short example of how we redact PII in logs?

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@fincopay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Data access controls / support access follow-ups

Hi Emily, attaching the break-glass runbook and a short audit-log sample here. Highlights:

- Authorization: Break-glass can only be initiated by Level-2+ support; production break-glass requires explicit customer security approval (AuthID logged).
- Duration & re-approval: Sessions default to 30 minutes and auto-expire; extension requires fresh approval.
- Audit format (single-line JSON-ish for ingestion): timestamp=2026-03-11T11:30:12Z level=INFO event=breakglass_start operator=svc-support-17 customer_approval=emily.chen@fincopay.com session_id=sg-5b9f ticket=RDW-TSK-789 affected_keys=3 redacted_snapshot=eyJrZXlzIjoiKGhyZWYpIn0=

Redaction approach: we store full request payloads in a customer-encrypted store and index only redacted tokens in logs; support sessions present a redact-first view. For customers that require zero plaintext exposure for PII, we can enable a redact-then-ship pipeline and provide hashed digests for traceability.

Attachments: Redwood_Support_Access_FAQs.pdf (runbook excerpt)

Proposed next step: 30-min tech Q&A Wednesday 3pm PT — Marissa, can you send invite? Emily, I'll bring a short demo of the admin view and a log walk-through.

Priyom
